heading: INT. SUGAR MILL - SECOND FLOOR - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SUGAR MILL - SECOND FLOOR - NIGHT
A long room of rotted grain sacks and a cold boiler.
A hole in the roof lets in the rain.
The three of them drop their packs.
The Captain spreads her map on a barrel and studies it with a pencil stub.
The Sergeant props his rifle at the window, rubs his knee, then looks out at the dark plain.
The Medic sits against the wall, unlaces his sodden boots, and winces as he peels them off.
How far to the bridge?
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: Fourteen kilometers.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: In the morning?
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: At dawn. If the river lets us.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: The river's already let us. It came up to meet us.
units.name: MEDIC

units.text: The Sergeant almost smiles.
The Captain doesn't look up from her map.
You'll want those feet dry, Medic.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: Yes, ma'am.
units.name: MEDIC

units.text: Then dry them. That's an order.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: The Medic wrings out a sock.
The Sergeant sits beside him and hands over a rag from his own kit.
Use this. It's clean. Mostly.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: MEDIC

units.text: What's your name, son? I've been calling you Medic for six days.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: Ibrahim, Sergeant. Ibrahim Osei.
units.name: MEDIC

units.text: Ibrahim. Good. A man needs a name in the dark.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: The Captain finally looks up.
A beat.
Something eases in her face.
Ibrahim, how old are you?
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: Nineteen, ma'am.
units.name: IBRAHIM

units.text: Nineteen.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: She says it softly, as if turning the word over to find out what it weighs.
Then she folds the map, takes a tin from her pocket, and pries it open.
Rations. One tin of peaches. We split it three ways.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: Peaches? Where did you get peaches?
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: I've carried them since the coast. I was saving them.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: For what?
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: For a night like this one. When nothing else was left to save them for.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: She passes the tin.
The Sergeant takes a slice and passes it on.
Ibrahim takes a slice and holds it up to the dim light like a jewel before he eats it.
It's sweet.
units.name: IBRAHIM

units.text: It is.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: Eat the syrup too. We'll want the sugar tomorrow.
units.name: CAPTAIN

units.text: They drink the syrup in turns, silently.
Rain ticks on the sacks.
Below them the water slaps against the vats.
The Sergeant takes the first watch at the window.
The Captain lies down with her pack for a pillow, her eyes open.
Ibrahim curls on his side, hands tucked between his knees.
Sergeant? Do you think we'll make the bridge?
units.name: IBRAHIM

units.text: Sleep, Ibrahim.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: But do you think...
units.name: IBRAHIM

units.text: I think the bridge has waited this long. It can wait for you.
units.name: SERGEANT

units.text: Ibrahim's breath slows.
The Captain closes her eyes.
The Sergeant stays at the window, a shape against the gray, listening to the rain and the river and, beyond them, nothing at all.
